decisive_patterns: paired-camera field designs can fail because public releases collapse pair-member identity
large multi-city or multi-study datasets can lack a separately identifiable detection channel
long-duration datasets can fail source/protocol crossing
distance-sampling outputs can be public while the independent reference-calibration object is not
strong geometry and replication do not rescue missing response-independent effort or detection identification

strongest_unresolved_reference.interpretation: unresolved is not pass; multiple camera models alone do not satisfy G4

reopen_E5_only_if_all: a candidate is surfaced independently of E5 focal response values or prior candidate outcome direction
public methods/schema/metadata already demonstrate a separately identifiable detection path before focal response opening
the detection/source/protocol factor overlaps at least two geographic regimes rather than being perfectly confounded with geography
public design metadata make the frozen physical-replication and six-month temporal requirements plausibly satisfiable
the candidate is not a repair or rerun of a previously stopped authorization

interpretation.supported: under the frozen E5 requirements, the screened public-data universe did not yield a design that independently separates activity from effective detection while also supporting strict geographic transfer
not_supported: CTDS or paired-camera methods are invalid
the E4 activity failure is causal or behavioral
